stm-2026-09-03|1|amending fy27 school bu.allowed: To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate an additional sum of Four Hundred Eighteen Thousand Fifty-Six Dollars and No Cents ($418,056.00) for the FY 27 operating budget for the School Department, or take any other action relative thereto AMENDING FY27 SCHOOL BUDGET $418,056.00
stm-2026-09-03|1|amending fy27 school bu.summary: This would add $418,056.00 to the School Department's FY27 operating budget, paid for by taxes. The School Committee asked for it, and the boards described it as extra state aid for the schools.

stm-2026-09-03|2|authorization to supple.allowed: To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, or transfer from available funds, a sum of money to supplement the School Department’s Fiscal Year 2027 (FY2027) operating budget, or take any other action relative thereto AUTHORIZATION TO SUPPLEMENT THE SCHOOL DEPARTMENT’S FISCAL YEAR 2027 OPERATING BUDGET
stm-2026-09-03|2|authorization to supple.summary: This would add an unspecified sum to the School Department's FY27 operating budget, either by raising it or by moving it from available funds. The School Committee said its lead sponsor would ask Town Meeting to pass it over.

stm-2026-09-03|3|supplement to the lunen.allowed: To see if the Town will vote to transfer a sum of money in the amount of $151,338.38 from Certified Free Cash or available funds to the Lunenburg Public Schools Fiscal Year 2027 Operating Budget for the purpose of supplementing the athletic department budget to reinstate middle school sports as well as provide transportation for student athletes; or take any other action relative thereto SUPPLEMENT TO THE LUNENBURG PUBLIC SCHOOLS FISCAL YEAR 2027 OPERATING BUDGET $151,338.38
stm-2026-09-03|3|supplement to the lunen.summary: A citizens' petition to move $151,338.38 from Certified Free Cash or other available funds into the schools' FY27 budget, to bring back middle school sports and pay for student athletes' transportation. The article's wording does not bind how the School Committee spends it.

stm-2026-11-17|10|advisory on stormwater.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17|10|advisory on stormwater.summary: This is a non-binding question from the stormwater task force. It asks voters to choose between paying for stormwater permit compliance through a stormwater utility or through the regular operating budget, and it decides nothing.

stm-2026-11-17|11|continuity of trust fu.allowed: continuity of trust fund administration during vacancy
stm-2026-11-17|11|continuity of trust fu.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17|11|continuity of trust fu.summary: Brought by the Trust Fund Commission, this article would set how trust funds keep being administered when a seat on the commission is vacant. The commission rewrote it after its lawyer's comments.

stm-2026-11-17|6|design and engineering.allowed: design and engineering for accessibility and park improvements
stm-2026-11-17|6|design and engineering.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
refused: figure(s) not in the warrant or checked figures: 20
stm-2026-11-17|6|design and engineering.refused_text: This article would pay for design and engineering work for accessibility and park improvements. The Select Board agreed on October 20 to include it in the warrant, but to vote it down.

stm-2026-11-17||authorization to pay exp.allowed: authorization to pay expenses from a prior fiscal year
stm-2026-11-17||authorization to pay exp.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17||authorization to pay exp.summary: This would authorize the town to pay bills left over from a prior fiscal year. The Select Board voted to include it in the warrant.

stm-2026-11-17||corrective zoning amendm.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17||corrective zoning amendm.summary: This article would make corrective changes to the town's zoning rules. The Select Board sent it to the Planning Board for review and a public hearing.

stm-2026-11-17||non-binding question on.allowed: non-binding question on TC Passios demolition   $2–3 million -- to demolish the building: a committee member's rough estimate, scaled up from the 2023 primary school demolition
stm-2026-11-17||non-binding question on.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17||non-binding question on.summary: This is a non-binding question: it asks voters whether the town should pursue demolishing the TC Passios building, and it decides nothing by itself. One committee member's rough estimate of the demolition cost is $2–3 million.

stm-2026-11-17||stormwater management by.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17||stormwater management by.summary: This would take the dollar fees out of the stormwater bylaw and instead point to the Planning Board's fee schedule, which the board can update. The Select Board sent it to the Planning Board for a public hearing.

stm-2026-11-17||the fiscal year 2027 omn.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17||the fiscal year 2027 omn.summary: This would amend the fiscal year 2027 omnibus budget, the town's main spending plan for this year. The Select Board voted to include it on the warrant.

stm-2026-11-17||transfer of funds to the.allowed: transfer of funds to the special education reserve fund   $300,000 -- requested from free cash, if certified
stm-2026-11-17||transfer of funds to the.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17||transfer of funds to the.summary: This would move $300,000 into the special education reserve fund, taken from free cash (leftover money from last year) if it is certified. The School Committee asked for it.
